chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-'Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, from al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'It has reached me that a daughter has been born unto you, yet it has displeased you — but what you have from her is a fragrant flower to smell, and her sustenance has already been provided for you, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was a father of daughters.'

key_terms.أَبَا بَنَات: Father of daughters — referring to the Prophet Muhammad, who had daughters (Fatima, Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, Ruqayya) and no surviving sons
key_terms.رَيْحَانَة: Rayhana — an aromatic herb/flower; used metaphorically for daughters as something beautiful and fragrant to enjoy
key_terms.رِزْق: Rizq — sustenance, provision; the Imam's point is that God guarantees the daughter's provision, so the father need not worry

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about having a daughter in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir who had just had a daughter and was displeased, reminding him that a daughter is a blessing — a fragrant flower to enjoy — whose provision is guaranteed by God, and that the Prophet Muhammad himself was a father of daughters. This hadith directly counters the pre-Islamic Arab custom of mourning or even burying daughters alive, reframing the birth of a daughter as a divine gift rather than a burden.
word_analysis: yet you are displeased with her

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Aasimy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Tumayli, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his father, form Al Jaroud Bin Al Munzar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘It has reached me that a daughter has been born unto you, so it angered you, and what is upon you from her is an aroma for you to smell, and her sustenance has been Sufficed with; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was a father of daughters’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-‘Asemiy has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Taymuliy from Ali ibn Asbat from his father from al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘I am told a girl is born to you whom you dislike. What has she brought upon you? She is a sweet smelling flower you enjoy and her sustenance is guaranteed, besides, the Messenger of Allah was a father of girls.’”
